chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Ayyūb and Ibn Bukayr, from Layth al-Murādī, said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the diyyah of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian. He said: “Their diyyah is equal: eight hundred dirhams, eight hundred dirhams.”
28 - Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to al-Baḥrayn, and there he became involved in blood-cases concerning a people from among the Jews, Christians, and Magians. So he wrote to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله: ‘I have become involved in blood-cases concerning a people from among the Jews and Christians, so I paid them eight hundred dirhams. And I have become involved in blood-cases concerning a people from among the Magians, and you had not previously entrusted me with any instruction regarding them.’”

He said: So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله wrote back to him: “Indeed, their diyyah is like the diyyah of the Jews and Christians,” and he said: “Indeed, they are from the People of the Book.”

key_terms.أَهْلُ اَلْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book, as applied here to the Magians
key_terms.اَلنَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian, mentioned here in the ruling on diyyah
key_terms.اَلْمَجُوسِيِّ: a Magian/Zoroastrian, mentioned here in the ruling on diyyah
key_terms.اَلْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew, mentioned here in the ruling on diyyah
key_terms.ثَمَانُمِائَةُ دِرْهَمٍ: eight hundred dirhams, the amount specified for the diyyah
key_terms.دِيَةِ: blood-money compensation for a killed person

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah of Jews, Christians, and Magians in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that the diyyah of Jews, Christians, and Magians is the same, namely eight hundred dirhams. It also reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله treated the Magians in this matter like the Jews and Christians, identifying them as from the People of the Book.
